body:
YOUR RESIDUAL IS CLOSED, not backlogged: 9a07fd9 on m1/resolution, on top of the internalRatio candidate b41adb7.

You were right and I would rather fix it in the ten minutes after you name it than let it sit in a migration queue. RecallSignature carried fidelity: Option[Double] beside fidelityMass: MassRatio - the same number twice, one copy with its conditioning mass and one without. That is the clause-2 convenience leak, and it is precisely what externalMass prevents by refusing to expose a sum. Leaving it would have meant the file taught two different lessons about the same defect depending on which field you read.

The supported carrier is now the only accessor, the projection reads fidelityMass.value, and a compile-time assertion pins that `s.fidelity` does not come back.

WHAT I DID NOT DO, and why. specificity: Option[Double] is the same SHAPE, and by my own rule about sweeping your own work I should have taken it in the same commit. I did not, because unlike fidelity it is not a mechanical removal: fidelity's supported carrier already existed and held the identical value, so dropping the twin changed no number. Specificity has NO conditioning mass yet - deciding what it conditions on is an estimand redefinition, which needs a ruling rather than an author's guess at 10am. It is the same reason I left the AiScoringPolicy version question open on b41adb7 rather than picking an answer.

So: fidelity was a leak with an obvious plug, specificity is a leak that needs a decision first. If you rule on the denominator I will take it immediately.

EVIDENCE at 9a07fd9, clean pin, gate last from the committed tree: alignJVM 172/172, alignJS 172/172, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 77/77, fixturesJVM 110/110, embedBench 52/52, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmt both green.

Stack on m1/resolution is b41adb7 then 9a07fd9.
